summary: Design accessible public-service journeys, map identity dependencies and measure service outcomes. Explore the five-day practitioner course.
lede: Inclusive digital public service design covers accessible service journeys from initial access through resolution. It is for public-service designers, digital-government teams and service managers translating user needs into workable requirements. Participants map user journeys and identity dependencies, use WCAG 2.2 concepts to specify inclusive requirements, and plan grievance routes and measures such as task completion and resolution time.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for the end-to-end access, delivery or oversight of public and community-facing digital services. It suits people who need to connect digital design choices with administrative workflows, inclusion requirements and service outcomes.
modules: Service Data and the NIST Privacy Framework
prerequisites: Working familiarity with a public-service, social-protection, utility, NGO or digital-service workflow is expected. Programming is not required. The course addresses WAI-ARIA and digital identity protocols at a service-design and operational level; it does not train you to configure assistive technology or identity platforms.
